title: Backfill Dry‑Run: cost & impact estimator service
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
The Console currently allows operators to schedule backfills and reprocess jobs, but customers frequently ask for a way to preview the *impact* and *cost* of a backfill before committing—especially for multi-tenant analytics pipelines where joins, schema changes, or transformation logic can amplify data volume.

Goal:
Build a Backfill Dry‑Run & Estimator service that simulates a backfill run in a non‑mutating sandbox and returns:
- estimated runtime (wall clock) and peak parallelism needs,
- estimated billable units / token cost and infra cost (GPU/hours, IO),
- sample output diff (row-level preview limited to N rows),
- expected downstream cardinality and bytes written,
- recommended shard/parallelism/throughput settings and safety guardrails.

Scope / Non-Goals:
- Scope: analytics pipelines powering Console usage metrics and alerts. Start with the eventstream->aggregation path used by per-route latency/cost dashboards.
- Non-Goal: full-fidelity replay that writes to production stores. This is a dry-run only; it must not mutate customer-facing tables.

Approach (high level):
1) Planner: take a backfill configuration (time window, tenant scope, transforms) and construct a sample execution plan.
2) Sampler: draw representative sample rows per tenant/time bucket (stratified sampling) and execute pipeline transforms to compute a projection of output size and transformation cost.
3) Cost model: combine sampled per-row CPU/token/IO estimates with cluster pricing (from infra pricing table) and runtime heuristics (batching, KV cache hit-rate) to produce an end-to-end cost & duration estimate.
4) Dry-run sandbox: run the pipeline on sampled data inside ephemeral read-only contexts; produce sample diffs and a trace-like summary.
5) Recommendations engine: suggest shard counts, parallelism, and safe commit windows; flag operations that require schema migration or manual approval.

Data flows / APIs:
- POST /api/internal/backfill/dry_run { config: {...}, sample_size: 1000 } -> { estimate_id }
- GET /api/internal/backfill/dry_run/{estimate_id} -> { runtime_estimate, cost_breakdown, sample_diff_url, warnings }
- Sample diffs stored for 7 days in internal S3 bucket; links require Console auth.

Acceptance criteria:
- Service returns estimates within ±25% of actual run for >80% of historical test backfills (validated against 10 past backfills).
- Dry-run never writes to production stores; e2e tests enforce read-only IAM role.
- Console UI can display estimated cost and a sample diff link for scheduled backfills.
- Generates recommended shard/parallelism and at least 2 safety flags when high-risk conditions detected (e.g., schema change, >5x expected output growth).

Implementation notes and decisions:
- Use stratified sampling (time + tenant weight) rather than pure random sampling to capture long-tail tenants.
- Cost model will be a hybrid: rule-based heuristics + small ML regression trained on historical backfills. Initial rollout uses rule-based so we can iterate quickly.
- Dry-run compute will run on a dedicated "sandbox" namespace (K8s project) with read-only DB credentials and strict egress rules.
- Store sample diffs and estimator metadata in analytics-internal.{env}.redwood.ai S3; index records in the existing backfill-metadata Dynamo table.

Security and compliance:
- Dry-run must obey tenant data access rules; PII redaction applied in sample outputs by default.
- Security review required: yes (KMS key usage, read-only role).

Testing and validation plan:
- Replay 10 canonical historical backfills in the dry-run and compare cost/runtime estimates.
- Fuzz testing with synthetic high-cardinality tenants to validate shard recommendations.
- Integration tests that assert IAM role prevents write operations (negative tests).

Rollout plan:
1) Developer preview for internal Console/backfill users (feature flag).
2) Beta for a subset of power users (tenants with low risk).
3) General availability with guardrails and quota enforcement.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: sample not representative -> mitigation: stratified sampling + allow operators to increase sample size.
- Risk: underestimating cost -> mitigation: conservative multipliers and a mandatory "safety buffer" recommendation.

Related docs and artifacts:
- Spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Backfill+Dry+Run+Spec
- Infra PR (sandbox infra): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482
- Prototype notebooks: gs://redwood-internal/backfill-dry-run/prototypes/estimator.ipynb

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus on the sampling strategy and cost model assumptions. We chose stratified sampling because of tenant skew in production.
- We intentionally keep the initial scope limited to Console analytics pipelines to reduce blast radius.

2025-08-03 - Data Eng review (Marcos Reyes): Agreed on stratified sampling; suggested keeping an instrumentation toggle to capture full-run metrics for model training.
2025-08-05 - PM review (Sofia Nguyen): Request to include sample diff redaction by default for PII-sensitive fields. Added to security notes.
2025-08-07 - Liam O'Connor: Spun up sandbox K8s namespace and wired read-only DB role. Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482

2025-08-09 - Engineering update: First end-to-end dry-run on sample window (2025-06-01..2025-06-07) completed. Estimated cost $12.3 vs actual run $13.1 (within target). Observed: KV cache hit-rate assumption needed adjustment.
2025-08-11 - Review feedback (Data Eng): Adjusted cost model to include IO amplification factor for join-heavy pipelines; updated acceptance criteria to ±25% over 10 historical backfills.
2025-08-12 - QA (Tasha Brown): Integration tests added to CI; failing negative-write test fixed (missing IAM policy). Ready for internal preview feature flag rollout.
